question: Why does Romeo and Juliet announce, in its opening fourteen lines, that the two lovers will die?
answer: To move the suspense from what to how. The prologue tells of a pair of star-crossed lovers who take their own lives; from then on every hopeful scene is watched with knowledge the characters lack. That gap, called dramatic irony, makes each near miss and each undelivered message hard to bear.
move: Telling the ending can make every step towards it heavier.
ask: When I already know how something will end, do I notice the moments along the way more?
source: Shakespeare, Romeo and Juliet, Arden edition, 2012
reference: William Shakespeare, Romeo and Juliet, ed. René Weis, Arden Shakespeare Third Series, 2012
